lines.text: One AI agent for every project? It edits the wrong repo, and by morning it forgets everything.
Agent R Q fixes both. Isolated workspaces, and learning that every agent shares.
Each project gets its own workspace. Ada names one billing, and points it at the repo's folder.
Codex connects, and billing turns green. The storefront keeps its own agent, Claude Code.
A billing task reaches only billing's agent. The storefront agent never even sees it.
Each workspace has its own key, too. If one leaks, reset it, and the other workspaces never notice.
Now the learning. Billing's agent spent an hour on a failing test. So before it finishes, it saves one rule: tests need Postgres on port five four three three.
Next day, a new task. The agent reads the memory first, and starts on the right port.
Fork the workspace for a second agent, and it shares that memory. What one learns, the other knows.
Two agents saving at once? A stale save is refused, so nothing gets overwritten.
Playbooks become skills. Import them from GitHub, or let an agent write one from work it just did.
Keep one copy, and switch it on in each workspace that needs it.
When an agent finds a missing step, it saves version two. Every workspace gets the fix at once.
Isolated workspaces, shared learning. What does your agent relearn every morning? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
